mainTopic: When a new owner forbids carrying, ביטול רשות on שבת according to בית שמאי and בית הלל, and when a partnership in wine or oil replaces an עירוב
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא about a גר with no heirs who dies, leaving his property הפקר in a shared courtyard. The גמרא finds both clauses worded backwards. Each time, רב פפא proposes a new reading, and then the גמרא explains the original words: what matters is whether the property could have been taken before שבת began. The גמרא then asks why the new owner forbids carrying when he could do ביטול רשות. One answer is that he forbids only until he does ביטול. רבי יוחנן answers instead that the ברייתא follows בית שמאי, who allow no ביטול רשות on שבת. עולא explains בית הלל's lenient view with 'כלך אצל יפות', but אביי refutes him. The גמרא concludes that בית שמאי see ביטול as acquiring a domain, while בית הלל see it as merely stepping away from one. A new משנה then rules that a homeowner who is partners in wine with each neighbor needs no עירוב, though wine with one and oil with the other does need one, while רבי שמעון is lenient in both cases. The גמרא discusses רב's 'one vessel' condition and explains רבי שמעון as speaking of a courtyard between two מבואות. In that case each neighbor is permitted with the homeowner, but the neighbors still need an עירוב with each other.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא about a גר who died
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states two rules. If the גר died before שבת, whoever takes his property is אוסר. If he died after nightfall, there is no prohibition at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If the גר died while it was still day,] even though another Jew took possession of his property, he forbids carrying. If he died after nightfall, even though no other Jew took possession, he does not forbid carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא in the middle. It gives the ruling for a גר who died before שבת and for one who died after שבת started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר with no heirs leaves his property הפקר, so any Jew can grab it and become a new 'resident' who did not join the עירוב. If this happens before שבת, he is אוסר. If the גר died after nightfall, carrying was already permitted when שבת began, so it stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert. If he has no Jewish children, his property becomes ownerless when he dies.
Took possession, acquiring ownerless property by an act of ownership
His property
Forbids, meaning he makes carrying in the courtyard prohibited
From when it became dark, after שבת began

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'אף על פי שהחזיק' look strange here. If taking possession is what creates the new owner who forbids, why say 'even though' he took it? That is exactly the problem the גמרא raises next.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֶחֱזִיק יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֵר בִּנְכָסָיו —
phrases.english: Even though a different Jew took possession of his property
phrases.notes: This refers to a גר who died while it was still day.

phrases.english: he forbids [carrying].

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁחָשֵׁיכָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְזִיק
phrases.english: [If he died] after nightfall, even though [another] did not take possession
phrases.notes: The words 'even though' make it sound like nobody had taken the property yet.

phrases.english: a different Jew, he does not forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֶחֱזִיק יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֵר בִּנְכָסָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues a ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the גר died before שבת, the one who takes his property is אוסר. If he died after nightfall, there is no prohibition.

steps.title: The ברייתא contradicts itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the phrase 'even though he took possession' implies that not taking possession would forbid even more. Logically, the opposite is true.
steps.simpleTranslation: This itself is difficult! You said: while it was still day, even though he took possession [he forbids]. That implies it is not even necessary to say so when he did not take possession. On the contrary, when he did not take possession, he does not forbid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the ברייתא. It says the wording makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Even though X' means X is the weaker case for the ruling, so the case without X would be obvious. Here, though, if nobody took the property, it is simply הפקר. With no owner, nobody is there to forbid. So taking possession is what causes the prohibition, not something that should weaken it.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult. The text contradicts itself.
While it was still day, before שבת began
It is not even necessary to say
On the contrary, the opposite is true

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said: while it was still day
even though he took possession [he forbids],
and it is not even necessary [to say so] when he did not take possession.
phrases.notes: That's what the words 'even though' seem to suggest.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּה, כִּי לֹא הֶחְזִיק לָא אָסַר!
phrases.english: On the contrary, when he did not take possession, he does not forbid!
phrases.notes: Ownerless property has no owner to forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'אף על פי שהחזיק' in the case of a death before שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Even though' wrongly treats taking possession as the weaker case. In fact, taking possession is what creates an owner who can forbid.

steps.title: רב פפא corrects the text
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא proposes reading the ברייתא as 'even though he did NOT take possession.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Say [the text reads]: even though he did not take possession.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the difficulty by suggesting the correct reading should say 'did not take possession.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the ברייתא says the person is אוסר even though he had not yet taken the property at a certain point. The exact meaning gets clarified in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the difficulty
Say, meaning 'read the text this way'

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְזִיק.
phrases.english: Say: even though he did not take possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the reading of the text (אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The text says 'even though he took possession,' which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The text should be read as 'even though he did not take possession.'

steps.title: But the text clearly says 'took possession'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב פפא: the ברייתא plainly says 'even though he took possession.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'even though he took possession'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב פפא's reading. The actual words of the ברייתא say the opposite of what he proposed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not want to simply change the words of a ברייתא. It needs an explanation that fits the words as they appear. This pushes toward the explanation in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches, pointing to the actual wording of the text

phrases.english: But it teaches: 'even though he took possession'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֶחְזִיק קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's suggested reading in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's actual words say 'שהחזיק,' the opposite of the proposed reading.

steps.title: What the ברייתא really means: he could have taken it before שבת
steps.stepSummary: If the גר died before שבת, a Jew who took the property only after nightfall is still אוסר, because he could have taken it while it was still day. If the גר died after nightfall, there is no prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: even though he did not take possession while it was still day but only after nightfall, since he could have taken possession while it was still day, he forbids. After nightfall, even though no other Jew took possession, he does not forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא so that both 'took possession' and 'did not take possession' fit. He did not take it before שבת, but he did take it after nightfall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is the death before שבת. At that moment the property was already available to grab, so this person counts as a potential resident from the start of שבת, even though he actually grabbed it later. If the גר died after nightfall, carrying was already permitted when שבת began, so nothing can forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. The text is explained, not changed.
But only
Since he had the ability to take possession

steps.whatToRemember: The deciding factor is when the גר died. If he died before שבת, anyone who later takes his property is אוסר, because it could have been taken before שבת. If he died after nightfall, carrying stays permitted, because it was already permitted when שבת began.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle of עירובין: the situation at the start of שבת decides the status for the whole שבת. Even a potential owner at that moment counts.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְזִיק מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
phrases.english: even though he did not take possession while it was still day
but only after nightfall,
phrases.notes: He did take possession, just later. So both readings fit.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְהַחְזִיק מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם —
phrases.english: since he could have taken possession while it was still day
he forbids.

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁחָשֵׁיכָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְזִיק
phrases.english: [If he died] after nightfall, even though [another] did not take possession
phrases.notes: The גמרא brings back the second part of the ברייתא, now reading it with this explanation in mind.

phrases.english: a different Jew, he does not forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by explaining the text as written, keeping the idea behind רב פפא's reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Took possession' and 'did not take possession' seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: He did not take possession before שבת but did after nightfall. He is אוסר because he could have taken it while it was still day.

steps.title: The wording of the second clause seems backwards
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'even though another Jew did not take possession,' which implies that taking possession would obviously be fine. The גמרא says the opposite is true: taking possession is exactly what causes a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: 'Even though another Jew did not take possession.' Does that mean there is no need to say it when he did take possession? On the contrary, when he takes possession, he forbids!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second clause of the ברייתא and attacks its wording. The phrase 'even though he did not take possession' seems to point the wrong way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Even though' (אף על פי) is used to introduce the harder case. Here, the harder case should be when a Jew DID take possession, because then a real owner is present who might forbid. Saying 'even though he did NOT take possession' treats the easy case as the hard one.

keyTerms.meaning: took possession (acquired ownerless property by an act of acquisition)
and it is not even necessary to say
on the contrary
he forbids carrying (in the shared חצר)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the actual text of the ברייתא here: 'אף על פי שלא החזיק' (did NOT take possession). The problem is that the word 'not' makes the logic run backwards.

phrases.english: "Even though he did not take possession,
phrases.notes: This is quoting the second part of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: another Jew" —
and it is not even necessary to say when he did take possession?!
On the contrary, when he takes possession, he forbids!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the second clause of the ברייתא stated earlier
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'אף על פי שלא החזיק' in the second clause of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Even though' should introduce the more severe case; but taking possession is more likely to forbid than not taking it, so the wording is reversed.

steps.title: רב פפא changes the reading
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests reading the ברייתא as 'even though he DID take possession.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Say instead, 'even though he took possession.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא fixes the problem by removing the word 'not' from the ברייתא's text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new reading, the logic works: even in the harder case, where a Jew took the property, if the גר died after nightfall there is no prohibition. The easy case (no one took it) is obviously fine.

keyTerms.meaning: say (read the text as follows)
an אמורא who often resolves textual problems

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Say:
"Even though he took possession."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by changing the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says 'did not take possession,' which makes the logic run backwards.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'did take possession': even then, there is no prohibition if the גר died after nightfall.

steps.title: But the ברייתא clearly says 'did not take possession'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא: the ברייתא's text says 'did not take possession,' so how can we change it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches: 'even though he did not take possession'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that רב פפא's reading does not match the actual words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא prefers to explain a text as it is written rather than change it. So it asks whether the existing words can be understood correctly.

keyTerms.meaning: but surely (introduces an objection)
it teaches (the text of the ברייתא says)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְזִיק״ קָתָנֵי!
phrases.english: But it teaches: "Even though he did not take possession"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְזִיק״ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's emendation
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's change of the text
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The written text of the ברייתא contradicts the proposed reading.

steps.title: Possession after nightfall does not forbid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means: even if a Jew took the property after nightfall, he does not forbid, because he could not have taken it while it was still day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: even though he took possession after nightfall, since he could not have taken possession while it was still day, he does not forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the ברייתא is really saying. It focuses on WHEN the property could have been acquired.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is whether this person could have acquired the property, and so become a resident of the courtyard, before שבת began. If the גר died after nightfall, nobody could have acquired the property while it was still day, so a person who takes it on שבת does not forbid. This matches the rule given earlier in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it means
from when it became dark (after שבת began)
while it was still day (before שבת)
he does not forbid

steps.whatToRemember: What matters is whether the property could have been acquired before שבת. If the גר died after nightfall, whoever takes the property on שבת does not forbid.

phrases.english: This is what it means:
Even though he took possession after nightfall,
since he did not have the ability
to take possession while it was still day —
he does not forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by explaining the ברייתא's meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The text seemed to require changing the words.
steps.terutzMaskana: Possession taken after nightfall does not forbid, because it could not have been taken while it was still day.

steps.title: Why can't the new owner just do ביטול?
steps.stepSummary: The first clause says the one who takes the property forbids. But why should he forbid? He should be able to do ביטול רשות, like an heir. This seems to go against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the first clause teaches that he forbids. Why does he forbid? Let him do ביטול!
steps.whatsHappening: With the ברייתא now explained, the גמרא goes back to the main issue of the סוגיא. It uses the first clause to challenge the idea that a person who acquires the property can fix things with ביטול רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If acquiring the property allowed ביטול רשות, the ברייתא should not simply say 'he forbids.' Its plain wording suggests the new owner is stuck. That would contradict the view, attributed to רב נחמן, that he can give up his rights.

keyTerms.meaning: in any case / at least
the first clause
why?
let him renounce (do ביטול רשות)

phrases.english: In any case, the first clause teaches "he forbids";
why does he forbid?
Let him renounce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wording issue and returns to the main debate about ביטול רשות
steps.kashyaTarget: The view (רב נחמן) that one who acquires the property can do ביטול רשות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא flatly says 'אוסר' and does not mention ביטול, which implies ביטול does not help.

steps.title: He forbids only until he does ביטול
steps.stepSummary: 'He forbids' means he forbids until he does ביטול. After ביטול, carrying is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he forbids' mean? He forbids until he renounces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading 'אוסר' more narrowly. It tells us what the word means in this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only tells us that the new owner causes a prohibition. It does not say the prohibition cannot be removed. ביטול רשות still works, so רב נחמן's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: until he renounces his rights
giving up one's rights in the חצר so others may carry

steps.whatToRemember: The person who acquires the property of a גר who died before שבת does forbid carrying, but only until he does ביטול רשות.

phrases.english: What is the "he forbids" that it teaches?
Until he renounces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of a term
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אוסר' means a prohibition that cannot be removed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אוסר' means he forbids until he does ביטול, so ביטול רשות works.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the ברייתא follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge to רב נחמן differently: the ברייתא follows בית שמאי, who hold there is no ביטול רשות on שבת at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whose view is this teaching? It is בית שמאי, who say: there is no ביטול רשות on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a new way to deal with the ברייתא that seemed to go against רב נחמן. He says it follows בית שמאי, so it does not reflect the accepted הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא implied that someone who takes over the property on שבת cannot do ביטול רשות. רבי יוחנן says that is true only for בית שמאי, who forbid ביטול רשות on שבת for everyone, even a regular owner. Since we follow בית הלל, רב נחמן's rule that an heir can do ביטול still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our teaching'; here it refers to the ברייתא being discussed
Whose view is it? (Which תנא said it?)
The school of שמאי; we usually do not follow their view
Giving up one's rights in a courtyard so others may carry there

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word מתניתין does not mean a משנה in our perek. It refers to the ברייתא the גמרא has been discussing, which seemed to go against רב נחמן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a very common move in the גמרא. Instead of reinterpreting a hard source, it says the source follows a view we do not follow, and so it does not count against the הלכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Our teaching, whose view is it?
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא that troubled רב נחמן

phrases.english: It is Beit Shammai,
who say: there is no renouncing of rights on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the challenge against רב נחמן raised in Step 10, in place of the reading offered in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a view we do not follow (בית שמאי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be the accepted halacha, which would mean an heir cannot do ביטול on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows בית שמאי, who forbid all ביטול רשות on שבת. It does not challenge רב נחמן, who follows בית הלל.

steps.title: The משנה where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about when to give away rights
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a משנה that shows בית שמאי require ביטול רשות before nightfall, while בית הלל allow it even after nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: From when may one give away rights? בית שמאי say: while it is still day. בית הלל say: even after it gets dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show that בית שמאי really do hold there is no ביטול רשות on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי say rights must be given away 'while it is still day', which means before שבת starts. בית הלל allow it after dark, on שבת itself. This proves the claim in Step 12 that, for בית שמאי, there is no ביטול רשות on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Giving away one's rights (the same as ביטול רשות)
While it is still day, before שבת begins
After it gets dark, once שבת has begun

phrases.english: As we learned: From when may one give away rights?
Beit Shammai say: while it is still day,
and Beit Hillel say: even after nightfall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's claim in Step 12 about בית שמאי's view.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that בית שמאי hold there is no ביטול רשות on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'מאימתי נותנין רשות', where בית שמאי require it while it is still day

steps.title: עולא explains בית הלל with the idea of 'כלך אצל יפות'
steps.stepSummary: עולא says בית הלל allow ביטול on שבת because the person is just showing what he wanted all along, like an owner who says 'turn toward the better ones'.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: What is the reason of בית הלל? The person is like one who says 'Turn toward the better ones.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל. עולא explains why בית הלל allow ביטול רשות even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of 'כלך אצל יפות' comes from the laws of תרומה. Someone separates תרומה from another person's produce without permission, and the owner then says 'you should have taken from the better ones'. That shows the owner agreed all along, so the תרומה counts. In the same way, doing ביטול on שבת only shows that the person always wanted the courtyard to be shared, so it is not a new act done on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'Turn toward the better ones': the owner shows that he agreed from the start
He is treated like one who says

phrases.english: Ulla said:
What is the reason of Beit Hillel?
He is like one who says 'Turn toward the better ones.'
phrases.notes: This comes from the laws of תרומה: when someone approves afterward, it shows he agreed from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind בית הלל's view in the משנה quoted in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For בית הלל, ביטול on שבת is allowed because it only shows the person's earlier wish to share the courtyard. It is not a new act done on שבת.

steps.title: אביי asks about a non-Jew who dies on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges עולא: when a non-Jewish neighbor dies on שבת, ביטול works, but there was no earlier wish to show, so 'כלך אצל יפות' cannot be the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If a non-Jew died on שבת, what 'turn toward the better ones' is there?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks עולא's explanation. He brings a case where ביטול on שבת works but עולא's reasoning does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the non-Jew was alive, the Jewish neighbors could not fix the courtyard by doing ביטול. Only once he died on שבת could their ביטול work. So the ביטול cannot simply be showing a wish they had from before שבת. Something new is happening on שבת itself, and עולא's reason does not explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew died
Is there?

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If a gentile died on Shabbat,
what 'turn toward the better ones' is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת גּוֹי בְּשַׁבָּת מַאי כְּלָךְ אֵצֶל יָפוֹת אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's explanation from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's reason for בית הלל ('כלך אצל יפות')
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the non-Jew dies on שבת, ביטול works even though it could not have worked earlier. So it cannot be explained as only showing an earlier wish.

steps.title: The real argument: is ביטול acquiring a domain or stepping away from it?
steps.stepSummary: Rejecting עולא, the גמרא explains the argument this way. בית שמאי see ביטול as acquiring a domain, which is forbidden on שבת. בית הלל see it as simply stepping away from a domain, which is allowed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here is what they argue about. בית שמאי hold that ביטול רשות counts as acquiring a domain, and acquiring a domain on שבת is forbidden. בית הלל hold that it is just stepping away from a domain, and stepping away from a domain on שבת is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'אלא' tells us the גמרא is dropping עולא's explanation. It gives a new explanation of what בית שמאי and בית הלל really argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about what ביטול רשות actually is. For בית שמאי it is like a transaction: the neighbors acquire my share, and acquiring things on שבת is forbidden. For בית הלל, I am just letting go of my rights, which is not a transaction, so it is allowed on שבת. This explanation also fits the case of a non-Jew who dies on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue
Acquiring a domain (like a transaction)
Stepping away from a domain
Merely, simply
It is fine, it is allowed

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: ביטול רשות counts as acquiring a domain, so it is forbidden on שבת. בית הלל: ביטול רשות is just stepping away from a domain, so it is allowed on שבת. Because we follow בית הלל, a ברייתא that forbids ביטול on שבת can be said to follow בית שמאי, and רב נחמן's rule stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. 'Acquiring' (מיקנא) is בית שמאי's view and leads to 'forbidden'. 'Stepping away' (אסתלוקי) is בית הלל's view and leads to 'allowed'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines what ביטול רשות is in הלכה: letting go of rights, not a transaction. That is why it can be done on שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, here they argue about this:
Beit Shammai hold
renouncing rights is acquiring a domain,
and acquiring a domain on Shabbat is forbidden.
And Beit Hillel hold
it is merely stepping away from a domain,
and stepping away from a domain on Shabbat is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts אביי's challenge in Step 15, drops עולא's reason, and gives a new explanation of the argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the argument (is ביטול acquiring or stepping away?)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל allow ביטול on שבת only because it shows an earlier wish (עולא).
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל allow ביטול on שבת because it is only stepping away from a domain, not acquiring one. בית שמאי forbid it because they see it as acquiring a domain.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For בית הלל, ביטול רשות is letting go of rights and is allowed on שבת. For בית שמאי, it is acquiring a domain and is forbidden.

steps.title: A homeowner who shares wine with both neighbors needs no עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a בעל הבית who is partners in wine with each of his neighbors does not need to make an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A homeowner who was a partner with his neighbors, with this one in wine and with that one in wine, does not need to make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It gives a case where a real business partnership in wine already counts as joining the households, so no עירוב is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב works by making all the households partners in shared food, so they count as one household. Here the people are already real partners in wine. That existing partnership does the job of the עירוב by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the core teaching the גמרא will discuss)
Homeowner
A partner who shares ownership
To make an עירוב, joining the households so carrying is allowed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the basis of an עירוב is shared ownership. A real partnership that already exists can count as one.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A homeowner who was a partner with his neighbors,
with this one in wine and with that one in wine,
phrases.notes: He shares the same kind of item with each neighbor.

phrases.english: they do not need to make an עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of ביטול רשות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partnership in wine with each neighbor replaces the need for an עירוב.

steps.title: Wine with one neighbor and oil with the other, and רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: If the shared items are different (wine and oil), an עירוב is needed. רבי שמעון disagrees and says no עירוב is needed in either case.
steps.simpleTranslation: With this one in wine and with that one in oil, they need to make an עירוב. רבי שמעון says: in both this case and that case, they do not need to make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the contrasting case: different items do not join everyone into one partnership. Then רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, the two neighbors are not partners in the same thing, so the three households are not one unit. רבי שמעון holds that any real partnership is enough, even if the items differ.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil
They must make an עירוב
Both this case and that case

phrases.english: With this one in wine and with that one in oil,
they need to make an עירוב.
Rabbi Shimon says:
in both this case and that case,
they do not need to make an עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to step 17 and records רבי שמעון's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: different items (wine and oil) require an עירוב. רבי שמעון: no עירוב is required in either case.

steps.title: רב: the wine must be in one vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the first case of the משנה: wine and wine needs no עירוב only when the wine is in a single vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב said: And it is in one vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב adding a condition to the first case of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, it is not enough that everyone shares wine. The shared wine must sit together in one container to count as a single shared item, like a real עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
One vessel or container

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav said:
And it is in one vessel.
phrases.notes: This refers back to the first case: wine and wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sharing wine replaces the עירוב only if the wine is in one vessel.

steps.title: רבא supports רב from the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the משנה's contrast between wine-and-wine and wine-and-oil only makes sense if the first case is one vessel and the second is two vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The wording is also precise, since it teaches 'with this one in wine and with that one in oil, they need to make an עירוב.' If you say the רישא is one vessel and the סיפא is two vessels, that works well. But if you say the רישא is two vessels and the סיפא is also two vessels, what difference does it make to me whether it is wine and wine or wine and oil?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to prove רב's condition from how the משנה is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine and oil can never be in one vessel, so the סיפא must be two vessels. If the רישא were also two vessels, the two cases would look the same, and there would be no reason for different rulings. So the רישא must be one vessel, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise, meaning it supports this view
The first part of the משנה
The later part of the משנה
Granted, this works fine
Well, fine

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is also precise, since it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: לָזֶה בְּיַיִן וְלָזֶה בְּשֶׁמֶן — צְרִיכִין לְעָרֵב.
phrases.english: 'with this one in wine and with that one in oil, they need to make an עירוב.'
Granted, if you say:
the first clause is about one vessel,
and the later clause is about two vessels, that works well.
But if you say:
the first clause is about two vessels,
and the later clause is about two vessels,
what difference is it to me whether it is wine and wine,
or wine and oil?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב's statement in step 19.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast in the משנה between wine-and-wine and wine-and-oil

steps.title: אביי: wine and wine can be combined even in two vessels
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבא's proof. The difference between the cases is not about vessels. Wine can be poured together with wine, but oil cannot be combined with wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Wine and wine is fit to be mixed. Wine and oil is not fit to be mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's proof. He shows that both clauses of the משנה could be about two vessels and still have different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two jugs of wine can be poured into one, so they count as one shared unit even while apart. Wine and oil can never be combined, so they stay two separate partnerships. This gives a reason for the difference without needing רב's 'one vessel' condition.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him
Fit to be mixed together

steps.confusionAlert: אביי only rejects רבא's proof from the wording. He does not necessarily reject רב's ruling itself.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה rules that a shared item replaces an עירוב. רב requires one vessel. רבא's proof for רב is rejected by אביי, who says wine-and-wine counts as one unit because it can be mixed, while wine-and-oil cannot.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Wine and wine is fit to be mixed together.
Wine and oil is not fit to be mixed together.
phrases.notes: In this line, לערב means 'to mix,' a play on the word used for making an עירוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: יַיִן וָיַיִן רָאוּי לְעָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבא's proof from the wording, not רב's ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The difference between the clauses can be explained by whether the items can be mixed, not by the number of vessels.

steps.title: How can wine and oil work together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's ruling again and challenges it: how can no עירוב be needed even when one partnership is in wine and the other is in oil?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: in both this case and that case, they do not need to make an עירוב. Even when he is partners with this one in wine and with that one in oil?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי שמעון's words from the משנה so that it can attack them. It asks how he can be lenient even in the wine-and-oil case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 explained that wine can be poured together with wine, but oil cannot be mixed with wine. So wine with one neighbor and oil with another should not join everyone into one shared unit. How, then, can רבי שמעון say no עירוב is needed?

keyTerms.meaning: Both this case and that case
And even (introduces a surprised challenge)
Oil

steps.confusionAlert: The quote of רבי שמעון is not a new ruling. The גמרא repeats it only to set up the question about wine and oil.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Both this case and that case
they do not need to make an eruv.
Even with this one in wine
and with that one in oil?!
phrases.notes: Wine and oil cannot be combined, so how do they join?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses אביי's point (wine and oil cannot be combined) to challenge רבי שמעון's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's leniency in the wine-and-oil case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different items cannot merge, so the partnership cannot unite everyone. An עירוב should be needed.

steps.title: רבה: a courtyard between two alleyways
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that רבי שמעון is talking about a חצר located between two מבואות. רבי שמעון is following his own known reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What case are we dealing with here? A courtyard that sits between two alleyways. רבי שמעון is following his usual reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question by redefining the case. He also points out that רבי שמעון has a known opinion that fits this case, and the next step brings it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בעל הבית does not need wine and oil to merge into one unit. He joins one alley with wine and the other alley with oil, so each partnership works on its own. His courtyard is linked to both alleys, even though the two alleys are not linked to each other.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a formula that redefines the case)
Alleyway / alleyways
Following his own reasoning
Courtyard

phrases.english: Rabba said:
With what case are we dealing here?
With a courtyard that is between two alleyways,
and Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wine-and-oil challenge by placing the case in a specific setup.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed all the neighbors must merge into one unit, which wine and oil cannot do.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each partnership links the middle courtyard to a different alley separately, so no merging is needed.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's three-courtyard case
steps.stepSummary: רבה cites רבי שמעון's ruling about three courtyards. The middle one can join each outer one, but the outer ones stay forbidden to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי שמעון said, what is this like? Three courtyards that open into each other and also open into the public domain. If the two outer ones made an עירוב with the middle one, the middle one may carry with them and they may carry with it. But the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source that shows what 'רבי שמעון follows his reasoning' means. It supports רבה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that one middle area can be linked to two different sides at once, without the two sides being linked to each other. Likewise, the courtyard between two alleys can join one alley with wine and the other with oil.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
What is this matter comparable to?
The outer ones
The middle one
Public domain

steps.whyThisMatters: It establishes the principle that one middle domain can be linked separately to two neighbors who are not linked to each other.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Shimon said:
To what is this matter comparable?
To three courtyards that open into one another
and also open into the public domain.
If the two outer ones made an eruv with the middle one,
it (the middle) is permitted with them,
and they are permitted with it,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁתַּיִם הַחִיצוֹנוֹת אֲסוּרוֹת זוֹ עִם זוֹ.
phrases.english: but the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for 'רבי שמעון לטעמיה'.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's explanation that a middle courtyard can join two alleys separately
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's ruling about three courtyards

steps.title: אביי: the cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that in the three-courtyard case the outer ones remain forbidden, but our משנה says no עירוב is needed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are they comparable? There it teaches that the two outer ones are forbidden. Here it teaches that they do not need to make an עירוב at all!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's comparison by pointing to the different wording of the two sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the three-courtyard case, some restriction remains between the outer courtyards. Our משנה sounds fully lenient, 'no עירוב at all,' which seems to permit everyone with everyone. So the comparison seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? (challenges a comparison)
There (in the other source)
It teaches
At all

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Are they comparable?
There it teaches:
the two outer ones are forbidden,
here it teaches:
they do not need to make an eruv at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison רבה drew in steps 23–24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's comparison of our משנה to the three-courtyard case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three-courtyard case leaves the outer ones forbidden, but our משנה says 'no עירוב at all,' which implies everything is permitted.

steps.title: What 'no עירוב needed' really means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'no עירוב needed' refers only to the neighbors with the בעל הבית. The neighbors still need an עירוב with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'they do not need to make an עירוב' mean? The neighbors with the בעל הבית. But the neighbors with each other do need to make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by narrowing the meaning of 'no עירוב needed' in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'no עירוב' is limited to each neighbor with the בעל הבית, our משנה matches the three-courtyard case exactly. The middle is permitted with each side, but the two sides are not permitted with each other. רבה's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Neighbors
With, together with
Each other

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, רבי שמעון allows the בעל הבית between two מבואות to partner with one side in wine and the other in oil. Each side is permitted with him, but the two sides still need an עירוב with each other.

phrases.english: What does 'they do not need to make an eruv' mean?
The neighbors together with the homeowner,
but the neighbors with each other
do need to make an eruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge and restores רבה's comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No עירוב needed' meant everyone is permitted with everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only the neighbors with the בעל הבית. The neighbors with each other still need an עירוב, just like the outer courtyards.
